bible_refs.note: εἰ δὲ ἔνθα που πέρ ἐστι τὸ Πνεῦμα, ἐκεῖ πάντως καὶ ἡ ἐλευθερία paraphrases 2 Corinthians 3:17 (οὗ δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα κυρίου, ἐλευθερία).
Lemma quoted in full (Ἡμεῖς δὲ πάντες ἀνακεκαλυμμένῳ προσώπῳ … καθάπερ ἀπὸ Κυρίου πνεύματος) and echoed again at the close of the row.

Moses' veil 'so that the sons of Israel could not look' follows 2 Corinthians 3:13; the quoted phrase τὴν δόξαν τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ is from 2 Corinthians 3:7. Background narrative is Exodus 34:33–35 (not cited inline: Cyril's wording follows Paul).
χαρακτῆρα τῆς ὑποστάσεως τοῦ Πατρός adapts Hebrews 1:3 (χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ); not set in quotation marks because Cyril names the Father and changes case.
διάκονοι καινῆς διαθήκης οὐ γράμματος ἀλλὰ πνεύματος, quoted (marked in the source).
ἐν αὐτῷ γὰρ κράζομεν Ἀββᾶ ὁ πατήρ matches Romans 8:15 (ἐν ᾧ κράζομεν· Αββα ὁ πατήρ); compare Galatians 4:6.
τὸ ἐρευνοῦν καὶ τὰ βάθη τοῦ Θεοῦ from 1 Corinthians 2:10 (τὸ γὰρ πνεῦμα πάντα ἐρευνᾷ, καὶ τὰ βάθη τοῦ θεοῦ).
LXX Psalm 118:18 verbatim (ἀποκάλυψον τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς μου, καὶ κατανοήσω τὰ θαυμάσιά σου ἐκ τοῦ νόμου σου); converted to Hebrew/English numbering 119:18.
Cyril's text adds λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι, reads ἀνθρώπῳ πλουσίῳ ('a rich man') for οἰκοδεσπότῃ ('householder'), and νέα for καινά. Translated as Cyril quotes it.
τὸν ἀῤῥαβῶνα τοῦ [Πνεύματος] with ἡμῖν matches 2 Corinthians 5:5 (ὁ δοὺς ἡμῖν τὸν ἀρραβῶνα τοῦ πνεύματος); compare 2 Corinthians 1:22. The quotation is cut at the row end and completes in u03-open.

choices.english: stands outside the bounds of slavery
choices.why: Perfect of ἀνοικίζω read as a present state; 'has been moved beyond' would imply the Spirit was once enslaved, which Cyril's argument denies.
Logical 'no longer' of the argument: if free by nature, then not among originated things.
The terse, close-packed letter of the law, not 'weakness'.
Cyril uses ἱερουργός of the apostles; 'priestly ministers' keeps the sacral sense without an archaism.
Litotes kept as a natural English understatement.

For it is Spirit of the Father, reaching (διήκω) from him to the creation (κτίσις) in Christ. [page 338] 'And we all, with unveiled (ἀνακαλύπτω, pf. ptc.) face (πρόσωπον) mirroring/beholding (κατοπτρίζομαι) the glory (δόξα) of the Lord, are transformed (μεταμορφόω) [into] the same image (εἰκών) from glory to glory, as from the Lord Spirit.' For Moses put (ἐπιτίθημι, impf.) a veil (κάλυμμα) on himself because the sons of Israel could not look upon (καθοράω) 'the glory of his face'; for they were soulish (ψυχικός) and fleshly (σαρκικός) and incomplete (ἀτελής) in faith (πίστις). But we the faithful, having the heart (καρδία) enlightened (φωτίζω, pf.) through the torch-bearing (δᾳδουχία) of the Spirit, and the eye of the mind (διάνοια) knowing how to see purely (καθαρῶς), with unveiled face have beheld (θεάομαι, pf.) the Lord; for he has spoken (λαλέω, pf.) to us and was seen (ὁράω, aor. pass.) in glory and most God-befitting (θεοπρεπής, superl.) pre-eminence (ὑπεροχή); for we have known (γινώσκω, pf.) him [as] God, impress (χαρακτήρ) of the subsistence (ὑπόστασις) of the Father. As in a mirror (ἔσοπτρον) then we behold (θεωρέω) the divine and unspeakable (ἀπόρρητος) nature; for the mind (νοῦς) of believers is as it were remolded (μεταπλάττω) from legal aptness-in-learning (νομικὴ εὐμάθεια) into gospel instruction (παίδευσις εὐαγγελική), and is transformed in a certain way into spiritual knowledge (εἴδησις πνευματική), not enduring (ἀνέχομαι) shadow (σκιά) or types (τύπος), but having chosen (αἱρέομαι, pf.) to pass over (μεταφοιτάω) from the glory according to the law into another glory, that in Christ, through the Spirit. Therefore we are transformed [into] the same image; for transposing (μεθίστημι) the types into truth (ἀλήθεια), and out of the shadow according to the law shaping (διαμορφόω) the mystery (μυστήριον) of Christ by the fineness (ἰσχνότης) of the conceptions (ἔννοια), we shall find the same glory as in form (εἶδος). For if glory has been given to those serving (διακονέω) the law, greater and incomparably (ἀσυγκρίτως) surpassing (ὑπέρκειμαι) the first is that of the holy sacred-ministers (ἱερουργός), who are also made sufficient (ἱκανόω) by God [as] ministers (διάκονος) 'of a new covenant (καινὴ διαθήκη), not of letter (γράμμα) but of spirit.' It is manifest (πρόδηλος) surely and unclear (ἀσυμφανής) to none of beings that wholly and altogether those being moved (μεθίσταμαι) from legal training (παίδευσις) to gospel exactness (ἀκρίβεια) [page 339] would be understood (νοέω, aor. pass. opt.) as going from the first glory as it were into another glory, and as being remolded as it were toward the better (ἀμείνων). And the [thing] moving them into this is the Spirit, which frees (ἐλευθερόω) from the slavery from the law; for in it 'we cry (κράζω) Abba, the Father' as sons (υἱός) and free. It is not [possible] otherwise to see the depth (βάθος) of the spare-speech (ἰσχνολογία) according to the law, except through the Holy Spirit alone; for it is also the one searching (ἐρευνάω) 'even the depths of God.' Depths of God we say is the name given to the knowledge (γνῶσις) treasured up (θησαυρίζω, pf.) in the sacred writings (ἱερὰ γράμματα); for this reason the inspired (θεσπέσιος) David made prayers (λιτή) to God, saying thus: 'Uncover (ἀποκαλύπτω) my eyes and I will perceive (κατανοέω) your wonders (θαυμάσια) out of your law.' And the Savior (Σωτήρ) himself made not un-marvelled (ἀθαύμαστος) the one ascending (ἀναβαίνω) from legal knowledge (εἴδησις) to spiritual, that is the gospel [knowledge]; for he said: 'Therefore I say to you that every scribe (γραμματεύς) discipled (μαθητεύω, aor. pass.) to the kingdom (βασιλεία) of the heavens is like a rich (πλούσιος) man who brings out of his treasure (θησαυρός) new and old.' Old (παλαιός) are the things in the law; new (νέος) indeed the things in Christ. But if someone should wish the transformation (μεταμόρφωσις) from glory to glory of our same image to be understood also in another manner (τρόπος), he will admit (παραδέχομαι) some such [thought] into mind: that as many as have known Christ and have been reckoned (καταλογίζομαι, pf.) among children (τέκνον) of God are wholly and altogether in glory; but at the time (καιρός) of the resurrection (ἀνάστασις) we are transformed [into] the same image from glory to glory as from the Lord Spirit; for Christ himself, to us, the one [who] 'the pledge (ἀρραβών) of the [cut off; continues in u03-open with 'Spirit, having granted']'.
pass_b_english: … outward narrative. For among these are those in Christ who have richly received the free revelation of the Spirit. And if wherever the Spirit is, there freedom surely is as well (2 Corinthians 3:17), how is the Spirit not free by nature? If that is so, the Spirit stands outside the bounds of slavery and is no longer something created, but would rightly be ranked with the highest and free nature, to which power over all things belongs. For the Spirit is the Spirit of the Father, reaching out from Him to the creation in Christ.

“And we all, with unveiled face beholding the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as from the Lord, the Spirit” (2 Corinthians 3:18). Moses put a veil over himself because the sons of Israel could not look upon “the glory of his face” (2 Corinthians 3:7, 13), for they were unspiritual and fleshly and immature in faith. But we believers, whose heart has been enlightened by the torch the Spirit carries, and whose mind’s eye knows how to see purely, have beheld the Lord with unveiled face. For He has spoken to us and has been seen in glory and in a majesty most worthy of God; for we have known Him as God, the exact imprint of the Father’s being (Hebrews 1:3).

As in a mirror, then, we behold the divine and ineffable nature. For the mind of believers is, as it were, remolded from its schooling in the law into the teaching of the gospel, and is in a certain way transformed into spiritual knowledge. It does not settle for shadow or types, but has chosen to pass from the glory that belongs to the law to another glory, the glory in Christ, through the Spirit. So we are transformed into the same image. For as we carry the types over into truth, and out of the shadow in the law give shape to the mystery of Christ by the fine discernment of our thoughts, we shall find the same glory as if in plain sight. For if glory was given to those who served the law, greater still, and beyond all comparison surpassing the first, is the glory of the holy priestly ministers, who are also made sufficient by God as ministers “of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit” (2 Corinthians 3:6).

It is plain, surely, and obscure to no one at all, that those who are moved from training in the law to the precision of the gospel would by all means be understood to be going, as it were, from the first glory to another glory, and to be remolded, so to speak, toward better things. And what moves them to this is the Spirit, who sets them free from the slavery that comes from the law; for in the Spirit “we cry, ‘Abba, Father’” (Romans 8:15) as sons and as free.

There is no other way to see the depth beneath the spare wording of the law except through the Holy Spirit alone; for it is the Spirit who searches “even the depths of God” (1 Corinthians 2:10). By “the depths of God” we say is meant the knowledge stored up like treasure in the sacred writings. That is why the inspired David made his prayers to God, saying, “Unveil my eyes, and I will perceive Your wonders out of Your law” (Psalm 119:18). And the Savior Himself regarded with no small admiration the one who rises from knowledge of the law to spiritual knowledge, that is, the knowledge of the gospel. For He said, “Therefore I tell you that every scribe who has been made a disciple for the kingdom of heaven is like a rich man who brings out of his treasure things new and old” (Matthew 13:52). The old are the things in the law; the new are the things in Christ.

But if someone wishes the transformation of our same image from glory to glory to be understood in another way as well, he will take some such thought to mind: all of us who have known Christ and have been counted among the children of God are by all means in glory; but it is at the time of the resurrection that we are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, as from the Lord, the Spirit (2 Corinthians 3:18). For Christ Himself, who to us “the pledge of the …” (2 Corinthians 5:5)

ἐμφανοῦς ἱστορίας οὐκ ἔχοντα. εἰσὶ γὰρ ἐν τούτοις οἱ ἐν Χριστῷ τὴν ἐλευθέραν τοῦ
Πνεύματος ἀποκάλυψιν πλουσίως εἰσδεδεγμένοι. εἰ δὲ ἔνθα που πέρ ἐστι τὸ Πνεῦμα,
ἐκεῖ πάντως καὶ ἡ ἐλευθερία, πῶς οὐκ ἐλεύθερον κατὰ φύσιν ἐστίν; εἰ δὲ τοῦτο, καὶ τῶν
τῆς δουλείας ἀνῴκισται μέτρων, καὶ γενητὸν μὲν οὐκέτι, συντάττοιτο δ' ἂν εἰκότως τῇ
ἀνωτάτω τε καὶ ἐλευθέρᾳ φύσει, ᾗ τὸ κατὰ πάντων μετέστι κράτος· Πνεῦμα γάρ ἐστι τοῦ
Πατρὸς ἐξ αὐτοῦ διῆκον ἐπὶ τὴν κτίσιν ἐν Χριστῷ. 338 Ἡμεῖς δὲ πάντες
ἀνακεκαλυμμένῳ προσώπῳ τὴν δόξαν Κυρίου κατοπτριζόμενοι τὴν αὐτὴν εἰκόνα
μεταμορφούμεθα ἀπὸ δόξης εἰς δόξαν, καθάπερ ἀπὸ Κυρίου πνεύματος. Μωσῆς μὲν γὰρ
ἐπετίθει ἑαυτῷ κάλυμμα διά τοι τὸ μὴ δύνασθαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ κατιδεῖν "τὴν δόξαν
τοῦ προσ"ώπου αὐτοῦ·" ψυχικοὶ γὰρ ἦσαν καὶ σαρκικοὶ καὶ ἀτελεῖς εἰς πίστιν· ἡμεῖς δὲ
οἱ πιστοὶ διὰ τῆς τοῦ Πνεύματος δᾳδουχίας πεφωτισμένην ἔχοντες τὴν καρδίαν καὶ
καθαρῶς βλέπειν εἰδότα τῆς διανοίας τὸν ὀφθαλμὸν ἀνακεκαλυμμένῳ προσώπῳ
τεθεάμεθα τὸν Κύριον· λελάληκε γὰρ ἡμῖν καὶ ὤφθη ἐν δόξῃ καὶ ὑπεροχῇ τῇ
θεοπρεπεστάτῃ· Θεὸν γὰρ αὐτὸν ἐγνώκαμεν χαρακτῆρα τῆς ὑποστάσεως τοῦ Πατρός. ὡς
ἐν ἐσόπτρῳ οὖν θεωροῦμεν τὴν θείαν καὶ ἀπόῤῥητον φύσιν, μεταπλάττεται γὰρ ὥσπερ
τῶν πιστευόντων ὁ νοῦς ἐκ νομικῆς εὐμαθείας εἰς παίδευσιν εὐαγγελικὴν, καὶ
μεταμορφοῦται τρόπον τινὰ εἰς εἴδησιν τὴν πνευματικὴν, σκιᾶς ἢ τύπων οὐκ
ἀνεχόμενος, ἀλλ' ἐκ δόξης τῆς κατὰ τὸν νόμον εἰς δόξαν ἑτέραν τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ διὰ
Πνεύματος μεταφοιτᾶν ᾑρημένος. οὐκοῦν τὴν αὐτὴν εἰκόνα μεταμορφούμεθα·
μεθιστάντες γὰρ τοὺς τύπους εἰς ἀλήθειαν, καὶ ἐκ τῆς κατὰ τὸν νόμον σκιᾶς τὸ Χριστοῦ
μυστήριον τῇ τῶν ἐννοιῶν ἰσχνότητι διαμορφοῦντες, ὡς ἐν εἴδει τὴν αὐτὴν εὑρήσομεν
δόξαν· εἰ γὰρ δέδοται δόξα τοῖς διακονοῦσι τὸν νόμον, μείζων καὶ ἀσυγκρίτως
ὑπερκειμένη τὴν πρώτην ἡ τῶν ἁγίων ἱερουργῶν, οἳ καὶ ἱκάνωνται παρὰ Θεοῦ διάκονοι
"καινῆς διαθήκης οὐ "γράμματος ἀλλὰ πνεύματος." πρόδηλον δήπου καὶ οὐδενὶ τῶν
ὄντων ἀσυμφανὲς, ὅτι πάντη τε καὶ πάντως οἱ ἐκ νομικῆς παιδεύσεως μεθιστάμενοι
πρὸς ἀκρίβειαν εὐαγγελικὴν, 339 ἐκ δόξης ὥσπερ τῆς πρώτης εἰς δόξαν ἰόντες ἑτέραν
νοηθεῖεν ἂν, καὶ οἷον πρὸς τὰ ἀμείνω μεταπλαττόμενοι. τὸ δὲ δὴ μεθιστᾶν εἰς τοῦτο
αὐτοὺς τὸ Πνεῦμά ἐστι, τὸ τῆς ἐκ νόμου δουλείας ἐλευθεροῦν· ἐν αὐτῷ γὰρ "κράζομεν
Ἀββᾶ ὁ "πατὴρ" ὡς υἱοὶ καὶ ἐλεύθεροι. ἔστι δὲ οὐχ ἑτέρως τῆς κατὰ τὸν νόμον

τὸ ἐρευνοῦν "καὶ "τὰ βάθη τοῦ Θεοῦ." βάθη δὲ Θεοῦ, τὴν ἐν τοῖς ἱεροῖς γράμμασι
τεθησαυρισμένην γνῶσιν ὠνομάσθαι φαμέν· ταύτῃ τοι καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος ∆αυεὶδ τὰς πρὸς
Θεὸν ἐποιεῖτο λιτὰς οὕτω λέγων "Ἀποκάλυψον τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς μου καὶ κατα"νοήσω
τὰ θαυμάσιά σου ἐκ τοῦ νόμου σου·" ἐποιεῖτο δὲ καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Σωτὴρ οὐκ ἀθαύμαστον τὸν
ἐκ νομικῆς εἰδήσεως ἀναβαίνοντα πρὸς πνευματικὴν τουτέστι τὴν εὐαγγελικήν· ἔφη
γὰρ ὅτι "∆ιὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς γραμματεὺς "μαθητευθεὶς τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν
οὐρανῶν, ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀν"θρώπῳ πλουσίῳ ὅστις ἐκβάλλει ἐκ τοῦ θησαυροῦ αὐτοῦ "νέα
καὶ παλαιά." παλαιὰ μὲν γὰρ, τὰ ἐν νόμῳ· νέα γεμὴν, τὰ ἐν Χριστῷ. εἰ δὲ δή τις βούλοιτο
καὶ καθ' ἕτερον νοεῖσθαι τρόπον τὴν ἐκ δόξης εἰς δόξαν μεταμόρφωσιν τῆς αὐτῆς ἡμῶν

καταλελογίσμεθα δὲ καὶ ἐν τέκνοις Θεοῦ, πάντη τε καὶ πάντως ἐσμὲν ἐν δόξῃ· κατὰ δέ

review_notes: Opens mid-sentence: ἐμφανοῦς ἱστορίας οὐκ ἔχοντα completes the last clause of u02-rem-mid (…τὸν ἱερὸν ὄψονται Μωσέα τὸ ἐκ τοῦ γράμματος προσωπεῖον ἤτοι κατασκίασμα τὸ ἐκ τῆς | ἐμφανοῦς ἱστορίας οὐκ ἔχοντα, 'they will see holy Moses no longer wearing the mask from the letter, the shadow cast by the outward narrative'; the negation οὐκ ἔχοντα is carried in u02-rem-mid's 'no longer wearing' so the join reads cleanly). Only the words in this block are translated; the lost start is marked with a leading ellipsis.
Ends mid-sentence at ὁ τὸν ἀῤῥαβῶνα τοῦ; u03-open opens with Πνεύματος" χαρισάμενος. The verb is not supplied here; the paragraph ends with an ellipsis so nothing is added.
εἰσὶ γὰρ ἐν τούτοις may mean 'among these [who see Moses unveiled] are…' or 'in these words are meant…'; rendered 'among these are', the plainer reading.
Πνεῦμα is neuter; to avoid an 'it' that sounds impersonal and a 'He' that the Greek does not mark, the noun 'the Spirit' is repeated where English needs a pronoun.
γενητὸν μὲν οὐκέτι: 'is no longer something created', the logical 'no longer' of the argument (if free by nature, then not among originated things).
ἰσχνότης τῶν ἐννοιῶν / ἰσχνολογία: 'fineness of thought' and 'spare wording' (the terse, close-packed letter of the law), not 'weakness'.
ἱερουργῶν: 'priestly ministers'; Cyril uses ἱερουργός of the apostles (compare u04-rem-mid, Paul ὁ τῶν θείων μυστηρίων ἱερουργός).
ἐποιεῖτο … οὐκ ἀθαύμαστον: litotes, 'regarded with no small admiration'.
Possible allusions not cited inline: ὡς ἐν ἐσόπτρῳ θεωροῦμεν may echo 1 Corinthians 13:12; λελάληκε γὰρ ἡμῖν may echo Hebrews 1:2.

Page markers 338 and 339 and the trailing page number 8 are omitted. The Spirit-and-freedom argument at the head of this row reappears in a near-identical form at the head of u03-open; both are translated as they stand in their own blocks.
Divine pronouns are capitalised for clarity (He/Him/His for Christ and God).

Review: Placeholder row ('Rem CLOSEOUT') replaced by the staged translation, reviewed clause by clause against the source and fixed in tr0.json: opening join made readable ('… outward narrative'; old 'that comes from the plain narrative, not wearing it' was stiff, and the negation now sits in u02-rem-mid); ἀνῴκισται (perfect) rendered as a state ('stands outside the bounds of slavery', not 'has been moved beyond', which implied the Spirit was once in slavery: doctrine); γενητὸν οὐκέτι 'is no longer something created'; citation shape '(2 Corinthians 3:7, 13)'; 'held in no small wonder' made natural. Rest checked: sense, negation, agency, Scripture (2 Corinthians 3:17, 3:18, Hebrews 1:3, Romans 8:15, 1 Corinthians 2:10, Psalm 119:18 from LXX 118:18, Matthew 13:52, 2 Corinthians 5:5) all correct.
